extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners and third‑party requesters) involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing filings, examiner actions, conferences, amendment entry, issuance of Right of Appeal Notices (RANs), reopening prosecution, and appeals in U.S. inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of panel conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference will provide a forum to consider all issues of patentability as well as procedural issues having an impact on patentability. Review by more than one primary examiner should diminish any perception of undue influence and provide greater assurance that all matters will be addressed appropriately; all issues will be viewed from the perspectives of three examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference members should detect what the examiner in charge might have missed and provide a comprehensive discussion of, and finding for, each issue. Conferees will initial actions to indicate presence; if the conference does not confirm the examiner’s preliminary decision, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action. If the examiner in charge disagrees with the conference decision, the manager will generally assign the proceeding to another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to hold panel review conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is issued without panel review, the patent owner or third‑party requester must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of the failure to hold a panel review conference; any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of conferees’ initials will be noted; failure to hold a conference, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.951(a) — Patent owner one‑time submission after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: After an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP), the patent owner may once file written comments limited to the issues raised in the Office action closing prosecution and may include a proposed amendment to the claims (subject to §1.116 admission criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be filed within the time set for response in the ACP. If the submission addresses issues not raised in the ACP, it will be returned or expunged; no additional opportunity absent a granted petition under 37 CFR 1.183 waiving the one‑opportunity limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.951(b) — Third party requester one‑time responsive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent owner files comments under 37 CFR 1.951(a), a third party requester may once file comments responsive to the patent owner’s comments within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s comments on the third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party requester comments must be limited to responding to the patent owner’s comments, proposed amendments, and/or issues raised in the ACP; comments beyond that scope will be returned or expunged; replacement comments allowed only upon a granted 1.183 petition and limited to the original submission content.

rubrics_metrics.name: One‑opportunity rule for post‑ACP submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After an ACP, the patent owner and the third party requester each have only one opportunity to file comments under 37 CFR 1.951(a) and (b) respectively; any second or supplemental submission by either party after ACP will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a granted petition under 37 CFR 1.183 permits corrected submissions, those corrected submissions must be strictly limited to the content of the original submission; third party requester may then once file supplemental comments within one month of service of corrected comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file patent owner submission after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner submission under 37 CFR 1.951(a) must be filed within the time period set for response to the ACP; normally the ACP sets a period of 30 days or one month (whichever is longer) from the mailing date of the ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension may be requested under 37 CFR 1.956 but may not extend past six months from the date of the ACP. If an extension was obtained, examiner waits until the extended time plus one month expires before taking up the case for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify and develop issues prior to ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner and parties should recognize that reexamination may result in final cancellation of claims and that the patent owner cannot continue the proceeding by refiling or RCE; accordingly, all issues (including presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132) should be identified and developed prior to the ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to ensure the record is fully developed before the one‑opportunity post‑ACP limitations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limitation on patent owner post‑ACP submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner’s comments under 37 CFR 1.951(a) must be limited to the issues raised in the ACP; submissions addressing issues not already raised will be returned or expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification will be sent to the submitting party; no additional opportunity to correct the defect unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is granted to waive 37 CFR 1.951 one‑opportunity limitation. Corrected comments permitted only when a 1.183 petition is granted, and such corrections must not go beyond the original submission content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on third party requester comments post‑ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party requester comments under 37 CFR 1.951(b) may once be filed to respond to the patent owner’s comments, proposed amendments, and/or the issues raised in the ACP; comments beyond that scope are improper and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If comments were scanned into the Image File Wrapper prior to discovery of impropriety they should be expunged with notification. Replacement comments only via granted 1.183 petition and must be limited to original content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent owner not filing post‑ACP submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not timely file comments or a proposed amendment under 37 CFR 1.951(a), the third party requester is precluded from filing comments under 37 CFR 1.951(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) will be issued when time for filing patent owner comments expires and no patent owner paper was received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to challenge premature ACP (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner believes the ACP is premature, the patent owner may, in addition to comments, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (to challenge making the action an ACP) within the time period for filing comments under 37 CFR 1.951(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a 1.181 petition does not toll appeal time; patent owner is encouraged also to file petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 and request extension of time to file appeal brief where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner takes case up for action after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: If no patent owner submission is received after two months from the ACP (or after the extended time plus one month if extension obtained), the examiner will take up the case for action; similarly, if no third party submission after two months from service of patent owner’s submission, examiner will take up the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where both 1.951(a) and (b) submissions have been received, the case should be taken up for action as soon as possible. Case should be acted on promptly in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 314(c) special dispatch requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should issue Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no 37 CFR 1.951(a) submission has been filed, or where a submission has been filed and the examiner will not modify his/her position, the examiner should issue a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner’s submission included a proposed amendment, the RAN will indicate whether it was entered. If a submission is incomplete/defective, the examiner should notify parties in the RAN that the submission was not considered and no additional opportunity is available to correct defects because comments may only be filed 'once' under 1.951.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion and undue burden regarding entering proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is not required to enter a proposed amendment after the ACP; the examiner is encouraged to enter an amendment when the entirety of the amendment results only in an additional claim(s) being indicated as patentable, unless entry would cause an 'undue burden' on the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the examiner does not enter the amendment, the examiner should explain the 'undue burden.' Where the examiner enters the amendment, consider whether a RAN can be issued or whether prosecution must be reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and limits on amendments submitted after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple amendments submitted after the ACP: all except the first will be returned without consideration. A patent owner cannot, as a matter of right, amend claims rejected in the ACP, add new claims after ACP, nor reinstate previously canceled claims without satisfying 37 CFR 1.116(b), except in narrow exceptions (canceling claims, adopting examiner’s suggestions, removing issues for appeal, or requiring only cursory review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entry of a proposed amendment would withdraw a ground of rejection or indicate additional claims patentable, the amendment generally raises new issues requiring more than cursory review; examiner must indicate new grounds and address any third‑party comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments relative to RAN timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed any time after the ACP and prior to the RAN may be entered where appropriate; an amendment filed after the RAN will not be entered except upon a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 because 37 CFR 1.953(c) prohibits amendment after the RAN in inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner wants an amendment after the RAN, the examiner can reopen prosecution, enter the amendment, and issue a new ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and evidence submitted after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits submitted after an ACP are subject to the same treatment as amendments submitted after an ACP (i.e., not ordinarily entered and treated analogously to affidavits filed after a final rejection in an application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties will be notified in the RAN or other Office action whether such submissions have been entered/considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reopening of prosecution when examiner changes position
rubrics_metrics.description: When a submission after ACP is filed and the examiner decides to modify his/her position, the examiner should ordinarily reopen prosecution; a RAN cannot be issued until the patent owner has had the opportunity to address each and every rejection prior to the appeal stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution ordinarily reopened by issuing a non‑ACP Office action. Reopening is required where any new ground of rejection is made or any additional claim is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary reopening of prosecution based on equities
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should be liberal in reopening prosecution where equities make it appropriate, because patent owner cannot continue the proceeding by refiling; example: minor changes needed to obviate rejection where it would be inequitable to send claims to appeal over minor points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reopen where reopening would cause an 'undue burden' on the Office. If prosecution is reopened, third party requester may comment on newly‑found patentable claims after patent owner submits suggested amendment pursuant to 1.951(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) — nature and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon considering post‑ACP comments or upon expiration of the time for such comments, the examiner shall issue a RAN (unless prosecution is reopened). The RAN is a final action comprising a final rejection and/or final decision favorable to patentability, identifying status of each claim and setting a one‑month time period to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment can be made in response to the RAN in inter partes reexamination; if no notice of appeal is filed, prosecution will be terminated and the Director will issue a certificate under §1.997 in accordance with the RAN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and development required in the RAN
rubrics_metrics.description: The RAN shall set forth the grounds of rejection for rejected claims; the reasons why a proposed rejection is not made for decisions favorable to patentability; reasons for patentability of allowed claims; and advise parties of rights of appeal and consequences of failure to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing a RAN examiner should carefully review all grounds of rejection and findings of patentability, restate relied upon grounds/findings in detail, set forth the examiner’s position on arguments/comments so the parties can judge advisability of appeal, and point out which post‑ACP submissions have been entered/considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions regarding non‑entered amendments and interplay with appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment after ACP was not entered because it does not comply with 37 CFR 1.116, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting entry of the amendment within the time period for filing a notice of appeal or cross appeal (note: filing the 1.181 petition does not toll the time to file appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner is encouraged also to file a 1.183 petition requesting waiver of prohibition of an extension of time for filing an appeal brief and request extension of the appeal brief filing period until after decision on 1.181 petition. Third party requester may once file comments responsive to a 1.181 petition within 30 days of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative form and correspondence requirements for RAN
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTOL‑2066 should be used as the cover sheet for the RAN and the RAN should conclude with form paragraph 26.08 advising parties of right to appeal and paragraph 26.73 providing correspondence/inquiry instructions and filing channels (EFS‑Web, mail, fax, hand delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web filings must include certificate of transmission and comply with 37 CFR 1.8(a) and 1.6(a)(4) to be timely. Parties should direct correspondence to the Central Reexamination Unit; examiners are not to be contacted by the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on post‑RAN amendments and evidence (statutory/regulatory restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment other than canceling claims (where such cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims) can be made in an inter partes reexamination proceeding after the RAN except as provided in 37 CFR 1.981 or permitted by 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1); furthermore, no affidavit or other evidence can be submitted after the RAN except as provided in 37 CFR 1.981 or 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed after the RAN will not be entered absent a grantable 1.183 petition; examiner may reopen prosecution to accept amendment and issue a new ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner never issues NIRC after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an ACP has been issued there is no requirement for the patent owner to respond; therefore there is no situation where a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) can be issued after an ACP and prior to the RAN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if subsequent argument persuades the examiner as to all claims after ACP, a NIRC is not issued; instead a RAN is issued to provide third party requester opportunity to appeal allowed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited RAN request requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedited RAN request (37 CFR 1.953(b)) may be made any time after the patent owner’s response to the first Office action on the merits; the request must (A) stipulate issues are appropriate for final action, (B) have patent owner and all third party requesters join, (C) identify all appealable issues, and (D) identify and discuss the positions of the patent owner and third party requester(s) on those issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner determines no other issues should be raised, a RAN limited to identified issues will be issued; if other issues are present or need to be raised, deny the request and continue prosecution. The request does not extend time for any responses/comments due when the request is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing RAN
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner determines proceeding ready for RAN, examiner formulates a draft preliminary RAN and informs CRU SPRS/TC QAS, who convenes a panel review conference; conference members review patentability pursuant to MPEP § 2671.03 and, if they confirm the examiner’s preliminary decision, the proposed RAN shall be issued and signed with conferees initialing as 'conferee'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conference does not confirm examiner’s treatment, examiner must reevaluate and issue appropriate Office action. Conference should ensure case is ready for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and estoppel in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may appeal decisions adverse to patentability; third‑party requester may appeal decisions favorable to patentability. A third‑party requester whose inter partes reexamination results in an order under section 313 is estopped from asserting invalidity in later civil action on any ground raised or that could have been raised during the proceeding, except for newly discovered prior art unavailable during the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals to the PTAB are conducted according to part 41; notices of appeal and cross‑appeal must be filed within time provided in the RAN, identify appealed claim(s), be signed by appropriate party/agent, and fees paid per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1). Cross‑appeals may be filed within 14 days of service of the other party’s timely notice of appeal.
